description: Graphite with 90k CMC, default total 16 g/L. A common compact adhesion law uses adsorbed-CMC work to derive its reference force and free-CMC/prescribed-shear retention to reduce it. No free-CMC repulsive barrier or RE2 tail is active. Sliding parameters are unchanged; rolling strength follows current adhesion.

numerics._absolute_tolerance_reference: Retain the existing 16 g/L force/torque residual tolerances; solver iteration/substep limits and pass_max policy are unchanged.

rough_contact._current_adhesion_rolling: Rolling capacity and stiffness follow the current scaled attractive load; accumulated rolling history, rolling_length_m and rolling_yield_angle_rad are retained. No additional retention factor is applied to sliding or rolling.

cmc._concentration_units: Both concentrations are g CMC per litre of aqueous phase. Adsorbed and free inputs are independent; excess adsorbed input is capped, never transferred to free CMC.
cmc._saturation_reference: Gwag et al., ACS Nano, DOI 10.1021/acsnano.6c10201: apparent adsorption 0.37 +/- 0.09 wt% per particle mass (Gr+CB). Approximate reference conversion for this graphite-water model (neglecting the small CMC share of the paper's total solids): 0.0037 * 997 g/L * 0.44 / 0.56 = 2.8984214285714285 g/L aqueous phase. This is a converted model benchmark, not a directly reported 2.9 g/L measurement. Reassess this explicit reference if solids loading or material changes.
cmc._adhesion_model: theta=min(adsorbed_g_L/adsorbed_saturation_g_L,1); q=(1-(1-sqrt(q_sat))*theta)^2; W_eff=W_bg+q*(W_bare-W_bg). The compact reference contact force is pi*(a*a/c)*W_eff before free-CMC suppression; no independent contact-force override is used.
cmc._q_sat_reference: 0.33 is the agreed starting benchmark for saturated excess-adhesion retention, not a measured CMC constant.
cmc._free_cmc_units: free_g_L is already g CMC per litre of aqueous phase: 1 g/L = 1 kg/m3. It is not total CMC; do not subtract adsorbed CMC again or apply a solids-volume factor. Free CMC is never capped or increased by the adsorbed-input clamp.
cmc._shear_adhesion_model: p=clamp((free_g_L-start_free_g_L)/(full_free_g_L-start_free_g_L),0,1); R=1-p*(1-min(abs(imposed_shear_rate)/full_shear_rate_s_inv,1)). U=-pi*lambda_D*W_eff*R*delta/3*(1-(h-h0)/delta)^3 for h-h0<delta, zero otherwise. The same compact law fully replaces legacy interactions at every concentration. The whole energy is differentiated, including curvature forces and torques.
cmc._shear_adhesion_reference: Steady-shear phenomenological closure, not measured CMC bond kinetics and not a guaranteed 1 Pa s viscosity. At saturated adsorption the centered face-face reference force before suppression is about 327.873 nN. At the 4 g/L free benchmark it is shear-independent; at 16 g/L it is multiplied by 0.01, 0.1, 1 at 1, 10, 100 /s. Replacing the former 4 g/L potential preserves its adsorption-only contact amplitude, not its former well shape or RE2 tail.
cmc._initialization: The existing 10 nm placement clearance is retained. Nonzero CMC pair interaction ends at h0+attraction_range_m=3 nm; the hard-contact gap stays 2 nm.
